jp: 趣味[しゅみ]{は|wa-topic}何[なん]です{か|ka-question}。
en: What is your hobby?
why: か closes the polite sentence and turns it into a question.

jp: 公園[こうえん]{で|de-place}毎朝[まいあさ]走[はし]ります{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you run in the park every morning?
why: か makes a yes/no question; よ and ね would make it a statement.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]{に|ni-time}サッカー{を|o-object}します{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you play soccer on Sundays?
why: か at the end marks the yes/no question; よ and ね only assert or seek agreement.

jp: 泳[およ]ぐ{の|no-nominalizer}{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you like swimming?
why: か turns the polite statement into a question about the listener.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]、山[やま]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きません{か|ka-question}。
en: Won't you go to the mountains this weekend?
why: か ends the sentence as a question, here an invitation; a plain particle cannot close it.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}天気[てんき]{が|ga-subject}いいです{か|ka-question}。
en: Is the weather good today?
why: か marks the whole sentence as a question; よ and ね would make it a statement.

jp: 桜[さくら]{は/が|wa-topic}もう咲[さ]きました{か|ka-question}。
en: Have the cherry blossoms bloomed yet?
why: か asks whether it has happened; よ or ね would state or confirm it instead.

jp: この川[かわ]{で|de-place}泳[およ]い{でも|te-mo}いいです{か|ka-question}。
en: Is it all right to swim in this river?
why: か turns the permission pattern into a request for permission.

jp: 体[からだ]{の|no-possessive}調子[ちょうし]{は|wa-topic}どうです{か|ka-question}。
en: How are you feeling?
why: A question word like どう still needs か at the end of the polite sentence.

jp: どこ{が|ga-question}痛[いた]いです{か|ka-question}。
en: Where does it hurt?
why: か closes a question that already contains a question word.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]何時間[なんじかん]寝[ね]ます{か|ka-question}。
en: How many hours do you sleep every day?
why: か ends the question even though 何時間 already asks for an amount.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{の|no-possessive}試合[しあい]{は|wa-topic}どちら{が|ga-question}勝[か]ちました{か|ka-question}。
en: Which side won yesterday's match?
why: か marks the question; the question word どちら does not replace it.

jp: 犬[いぬ]{と|to-with}散歩[さんぽ]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you go for walks with your dog?
why: か turns the habit into a yes/no question for the listener.

jp: 冬[ふゆ]{は|wa-topic}スキー{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you go skiing in winter?
why: か makes the sentence a question; よ and ね would assert or confirm.

jp: 海[うみ]{まで|made-until}電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}どのくらいかかります{か|ka-question}。
en: How long does it take to get to the sea by train?
why: か ends the question; どのくらい alone does not close the sentence.

jp: 一緒[いっしょ]にテニス{を|o-object}しません{か|ka-question}。
en: Would you like to play tennis with me?
why: か makes the negative form a polite invitation instead of a refusal.

jp: 森[もり]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{に|ni-location}鳥[とり]{が/は|ga-existence}いました{か|ka-question}。
en: Were there any birds in the forest?
why: か asks whether birds were there; よ and ね would claim or confirm it.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]野菜[やさい]{を|o-object}食[た]べています{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you eat vegetables every day?
why: か turns the ongoing habit into a question.

jp: ゆうべ、よく眠[ねむ]れました{か|ka-question}。
en: Did you sleep well last night?
why: か makes the past-tense sentence a question about the listener's night.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}マラソン大会[たいかい]{に|ni-target}出[で]ます{か|ka-question}。
en: Are you taking part in next week's marathon?
why: か marks the yes/no question about the listener's plans.

jp: 少[すこ]し休[やす]みましょう{か|ka-question}。
en: Shall we rest for a bit?
why: か after ましょう turns the invitation into an offer: shall we?
